name: Pááfang
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Quackenbush, Edward M. (1968) From Sonsorol to Truk: a dialect chain, PhD dissertation, University of Michigan (Chuukic dialect survey covering Hall Islands/Paafang; not reachable online)

sources.citation: Ellis, S. James. 2012. Saipan Carolinian, one Chuukic language blended from many. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 440 pp. (open, ScholarSpace hdl 10125/100894)
sources.note: Names Pááfang (PAF) as one of Quackenbush's 17 sample communities but explicitly excludes it (p. 209: 'CHU will suffice for representing Pááfang.. that attention will have to come in a later study'); no Pááfang phonology; silent on stress (one passing remark about 'slight accent differences spread across the Chuukic atolls', not a stress rule).

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick H. 1984. Reflexes of Proto-Oceanic in the Trukic languages of Micronesia. In Byron W. Bender (ed.), Studies in Micronesian Linguistics, 259-280. Pacific Linguistics C-80. Canberra: ANU. (open, ANU Open Research hdl 1885/253372)
sources.note: Covers seven Trukic languages (TRK, ULI, PUA, MRT, PUL, STW, WOL); Hall Islands/Pááfang not included; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Jackson, Frederick Henry. 1983. The internal and external relationships of the Trukic languages of Micronesia. PhD dissertation, University of Hawaii. xix+460 pp. (open, CC BY 3.0, MPG PuRe Language Description Heritage item_401117)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: No synchronic stress statement for the Hall Islands (Murilo/Nomwin/Fananu/Ruo appear only in the island list and in reports of Quackenbush's and Bender's groupings, where Hall Islands speech is lumped with Lagoon Trukese). Only stress content is a historical reconstruction, printed p. 223 (p. 249): 'It is almost certain that Trukic had a pattern of alternating stress, beginning with the penultimate mora and assigning stress to every second mora to the left of that one' (Proto-Trukic, not Pááfang).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en, fr) 'Pááfang language' / 'Paafang'; Glottolog 5.x languoid page paaf1237
sources.note: Stubs; no phonology; only references are Ethnologue and Quackenbush 1968.

sources.citation: Sakiyama, Osamu. 2003. Comparative studies of Trukic languages in the Central and West Caroline Islands. In O. Sakiyama (ed.), Studies of Minority Languages in the Western Pacific Rim, 1-43. ELPR Publication Series A3-006. Osaka: ELPR.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative Trukic overview that may include phonological notes on eastern Chuukic varieties; coverage of the Halls unknown.

sources.citation: Dyen, Isidore. 1965. A Sketch of Trukese Grammar. American Oriental Series Essay 4. New Haven: American Oriental Society. xi+60 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Classic Lagoon Trukese sketch with a phonology section; Dyen (1949: ix) noted the Hall Islands dialect was identified with an eastern Lagoon dialect, so its stress statement is the nearest published proxy (identity caveat: chuu1238).

sources.citation: Rehg, Kenneth L. 1993. Proto-Micronesian prosody. In Jerold A. Edmondson & Kenneth J. Gregerson (eds.), Tonality in Austronesian Languages, 25-46. Oceanic Linguistics Special Publication 24. Honolulu: University of Hawaii Press.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Survey of stress/pitch accent across Micronesian languages including the Chuukic group; may report Chuukese/Hall Islands accent placement and is the standard comparative reference for Micronesian prosody.

sources.citation: Goodenough, Ward H. & Hiroshi Sugita. 1980. Trukese-English Dictionary (Pwpwuken tettenin fóós: Chuuk-Ingenes). Memoirs of the American Philosophical Society 141. Philadelphia: APS. (Introduction: phonology and orthography)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Authors explicitly include the Hall Islands within 'Trukese' (p. xi, quoted by Ellis 2012: 209); the introduction's phonology section is the standard statement of Chuukese stress and would be the fallback description applicable to Pááfang if no Hall-specific source exists (identity caveat: Lagoon Chuukese, chuu1238).

sources.citation: Quackenbush, Hiroko C. 1970. Studies in the phonology of some Trukic dialects. PhD dissertation, University of Michigan. 154 pp.

sources.note: Phonology thesis on Trukic dialects from the same Michigan project; if the Hall Islands dialect is among those treated it would supersede E. Quackenbush 1968 for suprasegmentals.

sources.citation: Quackenbush, Edward Miller. 1968. From Sonsorol to Truk: a dialect chain. PhD dissertation, University of Michigan. 226 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only primary survey with first-hand Hall Islands (Murilo) data across 17 Chuukic communities; its phonology chapter is the most likely place for any statement on stress/accent in Pááfang. Named by the earlier scan and by Glottolog as the sole descriptive reference.

sources.citation: Krämer, Augustin. 1935. Inseln um Truk (Centralkarolinen Ost), 1. Halbband. Hamburg: Friederichsen, De Gruyter. 369 pp. (German ethnography, Glottolog listed by Glottolog as an overview)
